audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicted itself across layers: every phases[N].side read "Skill" while every content win[N] read "Irelia". Seven rows, all disagreeing.
audit.why: The page rendered two different answers to who wins each stage. The full-layer ratings (5/10 early, 6/10 from level 6) plus diff EVEN / 5.5-10 support Skill early and a small Irelia edge later; the 53.01% win rate over 2328 games is a mild edge, not a dominant one.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 settle on Skill in both layers; rows 4-6 settle on Irelia in both layers, with every why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as 'Pack Your Bags' — a fabricated ability name — and dismissed as not changing the math.
audit.why: The ability is Hounds' Pursuit (R): 110/95/80s, 900 range, lock-on dash with an untargetable window, revealing on takedown, recastable for a shield. It is the single biggest spike in the matchup and it is the reason not to stand past your wave.
audit.corrected: Named and costed in spikes[1], mid, wants.foe[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent: Irelia's E grounds Naafiri's Eviscerate escape, and three of Naafiri's abilities grant untargetable frames that eat a committed W or R.
audit.why: Irelia E carries the grounding flag; Naafiri's W, E and R all carry untargetable. Eviscerate (450 range, 11/10/9/8/7s) is both her escape and her pack heal — grounding it is what turns a stun into a kill, and dumping burst into an untargetable frame is what loses the trade.
audit.corrected: Written into dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, phases[4].why, breakdown.carry and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only as a vague 'his sustain' clause.
audit.why: Eviscerate fully heals her packmates on a 7-second cooldown at rank 5, which is what refunds trades you win.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds timing named in breakdown.feeding and phases[5].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: 18 misgendered fields (Naafiri is she/her), 2 copy-paste bleeds, and breakdown.cooldowns with no digit.

edits.before: From levels 3-5 you keep winning skirmishes because your combo damage output, boosted by resets, exceeds what her hound pack can sustain over an extended fight. Level 6 gives her Pack Your Bags, a strong dash/execute tool, but it doesn't change the underlying 1v1 math since you can simply avoid overextending right as she hits it and continue punishing her cooldowns. You remain the aggressor in most lane interactions.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 sit even rather than won: Eviscerate is a 450-range dash on 11 seconds down to 7 that fully heals her packmates, so the trade you win gets refunded before you can go again. Level 6 gives her Hounds' Pursuit, a lock-on dive on 110 seconds with an untargetable window and a shield on the recast, so don't stand past your wave when it is up. Your own level 6 answers it: Vanguard's Edge grounds the Eviscerate exit.

notes: The level chart was fully cross-layer broken here — all seven phases[N].side read Skill while all seven win[N] read Irelia. I settled rows 0-3 on Skill (matching the 5/10 ratings and diff EVEN) and rows 4-6 on Irelia (matching the 6/10 ratings and the 53.01% win rate over 2328 games), rewriting every why to match. If the intent was Irelia-favoured throughout, the ratings and diffRating 5.5/10 need to move too and that is a call I did not make. UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION carried over from the mel matchup: content whys[5], spikes[2] and spikes[3] build around Trinity Force while report[8] prescribes Blade of the Ruined King into Wit's End. I left those three fields alone. The suspectNames hit on "Defiant Dance's" in early is a FALSE POSITIVE — Defiant Dance is Irelia's own W and the text is correct. Not verified from the kits: whether Naafiri's packmates independently trigger Irelia's passive stacks, and whether Irelia's E grounding prevents the Hounds' Pursuit dash as well as Eviscerate.
